Global X runs north to south. Portal moments and drifts include roof actions and the gravity factor for
the named combination. Each peak is traced separately. Global Z runs west to east, Y upwards. Face
moments are about the west/north floor origin. Loads act on supports. Columns and mullions span from
foot to roof, jambs cantilever from fixed feet, and roof edges span to collector nodes. The longitudinal
model assumes rigid collectors and tension-only straps. Check actual restraint, collector and foundation
strength, drag and member resistance separately. Final approval rests with the engineer.
Analysis assumptions and pending checks
Closed metal-clad gable with a ridge post at each end. Bases are pinned. Knee and apex joints are rigid
in the portal model.
C15019 purlins and girts span individual bays. Maximum row spacing is 1.2 m on the roof and 1.3 m on
walls. Bridging restraint is excluded.
30 × 1 mm G550 X straps occupy the first and last bays of the roof and side walls. Six Tek screws per
end have an assumed 1.4 kN resistance each.
The longitudinal model transfers net end-wall wind through rigid eave and ridge collectors. Frictional
drag, restraint forces and fixing slip require review.
WindLab uses the entered speeds, unit site and dynamic factors, and an assumed IL2 basis with 1/500
ULS and 1/25 SLS annual events.
Illustrative external coefficients are −0.5, −0.9 and −0.9 for roof field, edge and corner, and +0.7, −0.5
and −0.65 for windward, leeward and side walls. Local corner and roof-edge factors are 1.5.
Roof loads apply to horizontal plan area. Enter cladding and secondary steel in the permanent load. The
solver adds primary steel selfweight separately.
Wind coverage is limited to the entered direction and internal pressure sign. Other directions, opening
cases and site exposure require review.
Full member stability, connection resistance, anchor and foundation design are PENDING.
